key_insight: Postoperative imaging-based measures of residual meningioma disease predicted recurrence better than surgeon-reported Simpson grade, with volumetric residual tumor performing best.
clinical_relevance: For meningioma follow-up and research, report-derived radiological grading and residual volume may provide more objective and prognostic extent-of-resection assessment than Simpson grade alone.
method: Retrospective multicentre cohort of 912 primary cranial meningioma resections (2006–2025).
Postoperative MRI reports were harmonised with TF-IDF + linear SVM to derive radiological gross-total/subtotal grading.
Residual tumor was segmented on contrast-enhanced MRI and tested against recurrence-free survival with Cox models and sensitivity analyses.
evidence_signal: Agreement between Simpson and radiological grading was substantial but imperfect (74% absolute agreement; PABAK 0.61), and prognostic performance improved from Simpson to radiological grading to log-volumetry (optimism-corrected concordance 0.692, 0.733, 0.748).
watch_item: This is retrospective and depends on postoperative MRI/report quality and timing, so automated report-derived grading may need local validation before routine use.
paper_title: Redefining Extent Of Resection After Meningioma Surgery: a Multicentre Observational Machine Learning Analysis Comparing Simpson, Radiological and Volumetric Grading
